extracted.intended_audience: Cochrane managing editors, executive editors, coordinating editors, and peer reviewers involved in Cochrane protocols and reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial guidance for managing and conducting peer review of Cochrane protocols and reviews, specifying roles, required reviewer types, procedural steps, mandatory checklist items, and acknowledgement/conflict-of-interest handling. Focused on ensuring methodological rigour, relevance, and transparency in Cochrane Library content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of peer review — protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocols for Cochrane reviews are peer reviewed to ensure that the research question is valid, the methods suggested are appropriate, and to avoid duplication of effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may use peer review reports to ensure that resources are allocated appropriately; for example, to prioritise protocols that answer the most relevant questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of peer review — full reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Cochrane reviews are peer reviewed to ensure that they follow the published Cochrane protocol or that any deviation from the published protocol is sufficiently explained; to ensure the research question is still valid; to identify whether any relevant and important studies have been excluded, the clinical context is correct and up-to-date, the methodology is appropriate and the conclusions are based only upon the data available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing Editor responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Managing Editors are responsible for managing the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include selecting and inviting suitable peer reviewers (following Cochrane editorial policy); liaising with DTA Editorial Team for DTA protocols/reviews; keeping accurate records of invitations and declarations (compliant with data protection policy); providing deadlines; providing materials (guidance, checklist); ensuring peer reviewers complete declaration of interest forms; sending reminders; collating comments; handling communications; maintaining and publishing an annual list of the group's peer reviewers; collating and sending feedback to peer reviewers; and raising concerns with the Co-ordinating Editor or Executive Editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Editor responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Editor has oversight of the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure peer review is conducted according to current Cochrane editorial policy; ensure procedures are up to date and published; evaluate final drafts and ensure readiness for external peer review; suggest appropriate peer reviewers; review collated reports and advise authors on revisions; ensure all relevant peer review comments have been addressed; raise concerns with the Editor in Chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network Senior Editor responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting CRG Co-ordinating Editors in making decisions relating to peer review and adjudicating on matters relating to peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise any concerns with appropriate external bodies (e.g., institutions and funders). (Note: role duties need reassignment in the document.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor in Chief responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that the Cochrane editorial policy on peer review is up to date and in line with international conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudicate on matters relating to peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number and mix of peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Cochrane review must be peer reviewed by at least one clinical/topic specialist (with a minimum of one external to the editorial team), and one statistician/methodologist (who may, in some circumstances, be part of the editorial team). It is also expected that at least one patient or public peer reviewer be involved per Cochrane review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of peer reviewers and the mix of expertise should be appropriate for the topic and complexity of the Cochrane review. Multidisciplinary topics may need several clinical/topic specialists. Peer reviewers with different skills should be guided to look at specific aspects (e.g., methodologists to focus on methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional types of peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional peer reviewers may include content specialists, systematic review specialists, or information specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit additional types as needed to comment on the particular aspects of a Cochrane review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical/topic specialist — expected role
rubrics_metrics.description: A clinical/topic specialist is anyone with in-depth knowledge in the topic area covered by the review (often a clinician). At least one subject-specialist must be external to the editorial team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At protocol stage they should assess whether the research question is valid. At review stage they should assess whether the research question is still valid (and what changed if not), identify whether any relevant or important studies have been excluded, and determine whether the clinical context is correct and up-to-date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistician/methodologist — expected role
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Cochrane review deviates from standard methods or uses complex methods, it should be peer reviewed by one statistician/methodologist; this person may be part of the editorial team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the review uses standard methods, these can be checked by an appropriate member of the editorial team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient or member of public — expected role
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are expected to seek involvement from patients, members of the public, or other potential users of the Cochrane review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They ensure review questions are relevant to people requiring and accessing health care, and that meaningful outcomes and potential harms are considered. For protocols, they help identify additional outcomes of importance and check language so reviews are accessible, with jargon explained. In some cases, patients/public may also be topic specialists. Use Cochrane Engage and ACTIVE project resources to recruit them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields as a source of peer review expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Cochrane Fields have access to methodologists, clinicians, policy-makers, patients and members of the public with expertise relevant to their topic area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a review is relevant to a Field's scope, editors are advised to contact the Field to obtain a subject-specialist peer reviewer to ensure methodological and clinical issues are addressed and relevance to stakeholders maximised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study authors as peer reviewers — conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a topic field is small and it is difficult to find peer reviewers with expertise, it may be necessary for authors of trials or studies included in a Cochrane review to be invited to peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is acceptable provided at least one other peer reviewer is external to the editorial team and independent of any peer-reviewed studies included in the review. If a peer reviewer is an author of an included trial or study, this must be declared in the peer reviewer’s declaration of interest form and in the manuscript’s conflict of interest statement. Authors of the Cochrane review should be made aware that a peer reviewer was a study author when receiving peer review comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity from protocol to review
rubrics_metrics.description: It is highly desirable to use the same peer reviewers for the protocol, the full Cochrane review, and any updates of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not possible, send key points from previous peer review reports to current peer reviewers to avoid revisiting previous decisions (e.g., on scope).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review of diagnostic test accuracy (DTA) reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review process for Cochrane reviews of diagnostic test accuracy is managed centrally by the Central Editorial Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This central management assures scientific quality and manages limited peer review expertise for these reviews. See Internal and external review for DTA reviews in the Editorial Manager Knowledge Base for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to all identities visible peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Patients and members of the public are exempt from the all identities visible peer review process and may choose to remain anonymous; peer reviewers must still declare any potential conflicts of interest each time they undertake peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an editor believes anonymity is required for other peer reviewers because visible identities would significantly negatively impact peer review, they may apply to the Editor in Chief for a review-by-review policy exception, providing details and reasons. Approved exemptions must be forwarded to the Evidence Production & Methods Directorate with review title, date, number of anonymous peer reviewers, and reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions for editors when exceptions granted
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must inform author teams when an exemption is in place and that it has been approved, and forward approved exceptions to the Evidence Production & Methods Directorate with the required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RevMan/Archie guidance: when a peer reviewer remains anonymous, ensure the peer reviewer has been assigned a Group role of 'Peer reviewer'; create a new Administrative note titled e.g. 'YEAR closed peer review submitted'; add the protocol/review name in the Note text; use Advanced Search in Archie to find closed peer review submissions as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inviting peer reviewers — invitation content
rubrics_metrics.description: The invitation email should contain the title and abstract of the Cochrane review (or title only if a protocol); deadline for return of comments; a statement that all information shared is confidential; and a link to the Cochrane conflict of interest policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-up email (after acceptance) could include: published protocol (for reviews); title proposal/registration form (for protocols); full manuscript (shared only after invitation accepted); screening documents if available; review-specific information (completed data extraction forms, included/excluded studies). Also include peer review checklist, contact details, specific peer reviewer guidance (if first time), and link to editorial policy on peer review (peer reviewer conduct). Inform prospective reviewers that acceptance implies consent for details to be stored in the Cochrane peer reviewer database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Cochrane Engage to find peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Cochrane Engage can be used to find new peer reviewers including patient and public peer reviewers, clinical specialists, and methodologists, or to advertise new peer review tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point interested individuals to Cochrane Engage to complete a profile; this is the route for potential peer reviewers being sign-posted on cochrane.org (Become a Cochrane peer reviewer). For additional approaches for finding patient and public peer reviewers, see SOP Section 2.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewers delegating responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Delegation of peer review responsibilities to junior staff members is permitted under certain circumstances (e.g., training/mentoring when junior is a subject expert).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invited peer reviewer must request permission from the Central Editorial Service and provide the junior's full name and contact details (position and institutional email) for appropriate acknowledgement. The invited reviewer must sign-off and take responsibility for the final report. Both original and delegated reviewers must submit completed declaration of interest forms and 'Permissions' statements from the peer review checklist; both may be acknowledged in permitted ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer declarations of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers must declare and describe any present or past affiliations or other involvement in any organization or entity with a potential financial interest in the outcome of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Cochrane's Conflict of interest policy for Cochrane Library content (2020) for what should be declared and complete the Cochrane declaration of interest form. Editors are responsible for assessing declared interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collating peer review comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review comments should be collated before sending to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should ensure that names and affiliations are included for those participating in all identities visible peer review, and removed for those not participating in all identities visible peer review. Record and send collated comments accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring authors address peer review comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor with sign-off responsibility for the Cochrane Library article is responsible for ensuring that authors have considered and incorporated any relevant and reasonable peer reviewers' comments that they receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are under no obligation to undertake further editorial steps until they can check the revised version meets the peer reviewers' requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback to peer reviewers and mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing comments and feedback to peer reviewers should improve the quality of peer review reports over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback is valuable to new peer reviewers and can incentivise continued engagement. For patient and public peer reviewers, consider implementing a mentoring system with experienced reviewers supporting newer ones. When requested, editors should provide peer reviewers with a copy of the authors’ responses to their peer-review comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledging peer reviewers in published article
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should be offered the option of acknowledgement in the article to which they contributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include text in the Acknowledgements section, e.g.: 'The authors [or the editors] are grateful to the following peer reviewers for their time and comments: [Insert peer reviewer names and affiliations].' For reviewers who choose not to be publicly acknowledged, indicate how many peer reviewers were involved and how many chose not to be publicly acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other forms of acknowledgement and reviewer credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers may receive payment in some circumstances, certificates, Cochrane Membership credits, and may record reviews via services such as Publons and ORCID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment is at the discretion of the CRG (e.g., for rapid reviews or specialist input). Certificates can support CPD/CPE. Peer reviewers can earn Cochrane Membership through completing tasks. Publons can provide credits; Cochrane reviewers can forward acknowledgement emails to Publons. Do NOT upload peer review reports of unpublished Cochrane reviews or confidential comments to Publons. ORCID can record peer review activity via services such as Publons or manually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review checklists and mandatory sections/statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cochrane peer review checklists (which can be used and modified) provide structured questions to guide peer reviewers. Available checklists include intervention protocol, intervention review, consumer versions, overview protocol and overview review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not using standard checklists, materials sent to peer reviewers must include mandatory sections/statements: Permissions (willingness to be acknowledged in published Protocol/Review and on the CRG/DTA website, with name/affiliation if Yes) and Potential conflicts of interest (declare present/past affiliations or involvement; complete the Cochrane declaration of interest form; Yes/No and details). Notes for prospective peer reviewer must also include confidentiality statement, that peer reviewer comments may be edited for clarity/consistency, and that acceptance implies consent for storage of peer reviewer details in the Cochrane peer reviewer database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support resources for peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: External resources to guide peer review are identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Committee on Publication Ethics: Peer review guidance; ICMJE recommendations: Responsibilities in the submission and peer review process (including responsibilities of peer reviewers). Cochrane peer review checklists and guidance notes for consumer peer reviewers are also referenced.
